propositions: A transient git fetch hang from the GitHub mirror causes subprocess.TimeoutExpired to be converted to SnapshotFetchError, which is caught by adapter's blanket exception handler and returns a spurious BLOCK decision indistinguishable from a genuine review fault

The spurious BLOCK vote (-1) is posted to Gerrit and recorded in the dedup store, permanently removing the change from backfill reconciliation because reconcile.py skips changes that already have an LLM-Review vote

The existing outer layer (app.py, reconcile.py) correctly handles retryable infrastructure faults by not voting and letting backfill retry, but the inner adapter layer is inconsistent and votes fail-closed instead

A narrow classifier is needed to distinguish retryable infrastructure faults (SnapshotFetchError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) from genuine review conclusions, and route infrastructure faults to an ABSTAIN result with no vote and no dedup row
An abstained review must emit a VOTER_ERROR marker for observability but must not vote or create a dedup row, restoring the change to backfill eligibility on the next pass
